incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike on /v1/generate in us-east-1 · error rate 5xx ↑ 8% · deploy 2026-03-14T18:03UTC suspected

alex (oncall): seeing the alert dashboard. p95 jumped from 230ms -> 2.4s in the last 5m. p99 ~ 5.8s. 5xx rate increasing.

sam (runtime): confirmed. traces show a lot of `upstream timeout` from model-gateway to transformer-pool. error logs show `Read timed out` from backend hosts.

alex (oncall): did anything roll out at 18:00-18:05?

deploy-bot: release 2026.03.14-1879 deployed to us-east-1 at 18:02:13 UTC by ci-pipeline. Canary traffic 10% -> 100% at 18:03:01 per rollout policy.

sam (runtime): looks like the rollout bumped traffic to the new quantized runtime (q4f). Kernel scheduling differences causing higher tail latency when seq_len > 1024. stacktrace snippets:
```
2026-03-14T18:04:07Z model-gateway[pid=2345]: ERROR upstream read timeout after 30000ms for req c9a3...
2026-03-14T18:04:09Z transformer-1[pid=4123]: WARN kv-cache miss; seq_len 1280; fallback to full attention path
```

priya (sre): customer impact estimate? Are any tenants failing completely?

maria (support): Support queue: ~6 customers reporting timeouts for generation APIs in last 10m. Two accounts on Dedicated experiencing 5xx spikes. CS already DM'ing impacted users.

alex (oncall): given customer impact and clear correlation with rollout, request immediate rollback to previous release. Priority = P0.

sam (runtime): agree. Workaround attempts (tuning kernel, reducing max_seq) would take too long to test. Rollback now.

deploy-bot: Executing rollback -> target release 2026.03.14-1878 (previous stable). Running: `kubectl set image deployment/model-gateway model-gateway=image@sha256:... --namespace=prod-us-east-1`

alex (oncall): rolling back. Notifying infra to watch for request surge on previous hosts.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed at 18:11:02 UTC. Health checks passing. Canary back to 0% (previous stable at 100%).

sam (runtime): post-rollback metrics: p95 back to ~260ms within 3m, p99 ~430ms. 5xx rate dropping to baseline. Logging shows no upstream timeouts now.

priya (sre): great. leaving a gapless audit: timeline, coro IDs, and affected customer list saved to /incidents/1819004321/handbook.

maria (support): updated the impacted customers with rollback status and ETA for postmortem. One enterprise customer requested SLA hit assessment — forwarding to sales ops.

elaine (product): flagging for eval: quantized runtime q4f caused tail blowup on long sequences. We need a canary gating rule for seq_len distribution next time.

alex (oncall): formal handoff in 10m to jamie. Jamie — summary: rollback performed, metrics recovered, root cause likely q4f kernel path for long sequences causing stalls. Open action items: 1) collect full traces for 18:00–18:11; 2) reproduce in staging with longer seq_len workload; 3) add canary gating by tail latency and seq_len percentiles; 4) customer follow-ups for enterprise SLA.

jamie (oncall-next): ack. I will take the on-call shift and own follow-ups. Attaching the quick links: dashboards, traces, deploy diff.

sam (runtime): quick note: archive of logs & failing request ids uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/1819004321/logs.tar.gz. I'll start a reproducer in staging pinned to q4f and seq_len 1200+; will paste results here.

alex (oncall): closing active incident — mitigation succeeded with rollback. Marking for postmortem and severity review. Will create an incident tracking ticket and assign to runtime + product.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: 1819004321 · mitigation=rollback · duration=00:07:41 · severity=SEV2 (postmortem required)

jamie (oncall-next): noted. I'll pick up the postmortem draft and schedule a 30m triage in 2 hours.

maria (support): continuing customer comms. If anyone has a short note for enterprise customers about cause and rollback, paste here and I'll include it in the write-up.

sam (runtime): paste for customer comms: "We observed increased timeouts after a configuration rollout that changed the model runtime path. We rolled back the rollout to the previous stable binary; the service is healthy. We're investigating the kernel path for long sequence workloads and will follow up with a permanent fix and mitigations to prevent wide rollouts until seq_len tail performance is validated."

elaine (product): adding: "We will add SeqLen-aware canary gating and increase canary traffic ramp durations for runtime changes; postmortem report will include timeline and planned fix."

alex (oncall): thanks all — handoff complete.
